conventions.convention: Gauge data specify the actual compact noncommutative group, a smooth right principal bundle, smooth finite-dimensional unitary representations, and admitted minimum-rank bundle-sector codes. They select no connection, action, or quantum theory.
Fundamental vectors are derivatives of p exp(tZ); ω reproduces Z and obeys R_g*ω = Ad_(g⁻¹)ω. Vertical curvature is K_H(X,Y) = −v([hX,hY]).
The form bracket uses the full permutation sum divided by p!q!; consequently one half of [A∧A](X,Y) equals [A(X),A(Y)].
For s_j = s_i g_ij, local potentials transform as A_j = Ad_(g_ij⁻¹)A_i + g_ij*θ_L and curvatures as F_j = Ad_(g_ij⁻¹)F_i. These are section changes, not arbitrary global bundle automorphisms.
The associated quotient satisfies [pg,v] = [p,ρ(g)v]; therefore ψ_j = ρ(g_ij⁻¹)ψ_i and the induced derivative is dψ_i + ρ_*(A_i)ψ_i.

The Lie-group and principal-connection constructions assume countable choice; the bracket construction itself is choice-free. The supplied horizontal distribution is assumed, rather than obtained from an existence theorem.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC_omega and a smooth right principal G-bundle with principal connection form ω associated to H. The curvature Ω_ω = dω + ½[ω∧ω] is horizontal and Ad-equivariant and equals ω∘K_H. For local sections with s_j = s_i g_ij, A_j = Ad_(g_ij⁻¹)A_i + g_ij*θ_L, F_i = dA_i + ½[A_i∧A_i], F_j = Ad_(g_ij⁻¹)F_i, and dF_i + [A_i∧F_i] = 0.

Assume AC_omega and a supplied principal connection TP = VP ⊕ H on a smooth right principal G-bundle. The orbit differential ζ_p: Lie(G) → V_pP is an isomorphism, and ω_p = ζ_p⁻¹∘v_p is smooth, reproduces fundamental vectors, has kernel H, and satisfies right Ad-equivariance. Conversely, reproduction and equivariance determine H = ker ω.

Assuming AC_omega, a non-Abelian gauge datum on a finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth boundaryless manifold specifies a compact noncommutative finite-dimensional real Lie group G, a smooth right principal G-bundle P, a set-indexed family of smooth finite-dimensional unitary complex representations, and a set Σ of admitted minimum-rank bundle-sector codes with [P] ∈ Σ.

For smooth homogeneous forms with values in a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra, the normalized alternating permutation formula defines a smooth bracket satisfying graded skew-symmetry, graded Jacobi, and d[α∧β] = [dα∧β] + (−1)^p[α∧dβ].

Assume AC_omega, a smooth right principal G-bundle with supplied connection form ω, and a smooth finite-dimensional complex representation ρ. For E = P×_ρV with [pg,v] = [p,ρ(g)v], the local expressions dψ_i + ρ_*(A_i)ψ_i patch independently of the local sections to a smooth E-valued one-form and satisfy the stated Leibniz rule.

alerts.finding: Example, first paragraph: “Identify ... by ia↦a, so its local potentials A_i have holonomy exp(i∫A_i).” With the cited right-principal connection convention and defining character, a horizontal lift s(c(t))h(t) satisfies h⁻¹h′ = −iA_i(c′), giving holonomy exp(−i∮A_i) for a loop inside one chart. Equivalently, the associated derivative is d+iA_i and its parallel equation has the same minus sign. The displayed positive exponential is inverse holonomy unless an alternative convention is explicitly declared. The horizontal-lift equation is also given in Vákár §1.3.4, https://arxiv.org/html/2110.06334. This observation concerns the holonomy clause; the magnetic-flux calculation does not use that clause.

Proof 5.1 says, for X∈T_x(U_i∩U_j), to use “the path g_ij exp(tZ) with initial tangent X.” This path lies in G and has initial tangent d(L_gij)_e Z = d(g_ij)_x X ∈ T_gij(x)G, rather than X in the base tangent space. The subsequent differentiation formula uses the intended tangent correctly; the quoted phrase needs a typing correction.

seams_checked.note: Right principal conventions, sector codes, Cartan curvature, and representation derivatives are preserved. The Euler–Lagrange tangent-space wording issue is separately alerted.
Examples use the stated bracket normalization, section-change law, and local curvature formula.
Local connection and curvature inputs retain the right-action convention; formal graded extensions are separately specified.
Bundle-sector codes and smooth principal forms retain their meaning; compactification and physical action are additional inputs.
Optional gauge data are explicitly retained as context and do not supply a connection, action, or quantum measure.
The operator contract separately supplies a connection and uses F=dA+½[A∧A] and D=d+ρ_*(A).
The selected SU(2) representation data are compatible with the supplied gauge-data interface.
The explicitly chosen positive-i Hermitian-generator convention gives the displayed negative non-Abelian component terms and remains compatible with D=d+ρ_*(A).
A_μ=−igB_μ and t_a=iT_a yield the stated associated derivative; superspace structures are separately stipulated.
Fundamental components transform by h⁻¹, with the compatible positive h⁻¹dh term in A′.
The page-level prerequisite supplies gauge context; its symmetry definition makes no stronger claim about ordinary principal connections.

The Abelian curvature and Bianchi specializations are faithful, but the Maxwell example's positive-exponential holonomy clause conflicts with the inherited connection convention unless inverse holonomy is intended; see alert.
Associated quotient and induced derivative match; analytic determinant/Pfaffian geometry is separately supplied.
Adjoint fields use the real form of the complexified representation, and contracting Bianchi gives D_iB_i=0.
The connection-existence lemma verifies reproduction and equivariance before invoking the connection-form converse.
The page retains gauge-geometry context; its local graded coefficient algebra and BRST signs are independently defined.
Curvature transitions, bracket normalization, associated connection, and BPST patching use the supplied conventions.
Only the compact group and unitary representation inputs are reused; no continuum connection or sector is inferred.
Smooth right SU(N) bundles, associated quotient, and adjoint derivative conventions agree; stronger analytic and choice assumptions are explicit.
The trace-curvature use of Bianchi is valid. U(N) connections are allowed by the general connection supplier, which does not require noncommutative G.
